_comment: How LOCUS is computed. Every product_class, attack_surface and evidence_type in vocab.json must appear here or in the matching defer_ list; validate.py fails the corpus otherwise. A vocabulary value with no locus does not fail anything on its own, it lands silently in the default, and a label that is quietly wrong is worse than one that is missing.
_tiers: Evaluated in order, first hit wins. declared: how[].locus is set on a block, or, for a library pattern placed with no block, the pattern's own locus with its locus_reason. surface_supply: a supply surface, for a block that detects the supply path itself (see surface_vector_techniques); an exposure has no block, and its authored surface decides for the record. class_nonproduct: the FIRST-listed product_class is a non-product class, or every class listed is one; the record is then about an organisation type or a process, not a technology. A non-product class listed after a product class is a sector tag in practice and decides nothing. posture: the block's rule_shape is inventory and every evidence_type it reads, deferred and contested types aside, reads posture (vuln_scan, asset_inventory), so it is an inventory question, which the vocabulary places on ORGANISATION whatever class or non-supply surface its record carries (see _why_posture). surface: what.attack_surface commits to a locus, unless it is in surface_span_only, the record is an exposure tagged by a generator in untrusted_surface_tags, or the block has gone past the way in (see way_in_techniques). host_evidence: the surface was set aside for a block past the way in whose deciding evidence reads only host evidence (by_evidence ENDPOINT), and so nothing on the surface's plane or its first-listed class's; ENDPOINT decides and the surface is its span (see _why_host_evidence). operation: the block carries a cloud_operation, not every operation is in non_administrative_operations, and either every typed marker is a cloud_operation or the block reads only the provider's audit trail (its deciding evidence reads only MANAGEMENT, and cloud_audit is its only MANAGEMENT type), every other typed marker then being a field of the same audit event; its live test is a cloud or SaaS administrative API, which the vocabulary places on MANAGEMENT whatever the provider calls it (see _why_non_administrative_operations). admin_api_unread: the first-listed product_class is in administrative_api_classes and the block never reads that API: it carries no cloud_operation marker, and its deciding evidence reads one locus that is neither the class's nor posture; that locus decides (see _why_administrative_api_classes). admin_api_listed: a record's block reads nothing on its first-listed class's plane, reads the plane of a class in administrative_api_classes that the record lists after its first, and its cloud_operation markers, if it carries any, are not all uses of a service; that class's locus decides (see _why_admin_api_listed). host_listed: a record's block whose first-listed class is not on ENDPOINT reads only host evidence, and the record lists a class by_class places on ENDPOINT after its first; ENDPOINT decides (see _why_host_listed). Neither *_listed tier reads a library pattern placed with no block. identifier: a generated exposure every one of whose identifiers carries a what.identifier_signals locus entry, all reading one locus other than its first-listed class's: what each identifier's own catalogue or advisory text names decides, and the class's plane becomes the span (see identifier_reading). A class entry never decides here. class_first: the first-listed product_class, which is the primary subject the author named. default: CONTROL, the floor for an input carrying no mapped class, which validate.py refuses in the corpus, so the shipped corpus never reaches it. The inputs are per record except how[].locus, rule_shape, evidence_type, technique and markers, which are per block; a library pattern placed with no block reads its own rule_shape, evidence_type and markers in their place, as its applies_to_classes stand in for a product_class. evidence_type is never a tier on its own: it decides only in the test of whether a surface reaches the block and inside five tiers, host_evidence, posture, admin_api_unread, admin_api_listed and host_listed, each placing a block only where it reads nothing on the plane it displaces and all reading the same deciding set, deferred and contested types left out; it is otherwise the last span source.
_why_not_markers: Marker types in general were tried and rejected. Most markers are type=computed, whose expr is free prose and would need pattern-matching over English to classify, which is the same tautology coverage() already documents, and the typed remainder is too thin to move any label. One typed marker is the exception: a cloud_operation names the operation itself in a cloud or SaaS audit trail, which is the one thing the standing decision places, so the operation tier reads it and nothing else, admin_api_unread asks only whether a block carries one, and admin_api_listed only whether every one it carries is a listed use. Since the fourth validation the operation tier also places a block reading only the provider's audit trail whose cloud_operation sits beside other typed markers, because there those markers are fields of the same audit event, a user name, an agent, an outcome; their types are allowed beside the operation, never read for a locus.
_why_posture: Until the 2026-10-01 third validation a shape tier sat after class_first and placed an inventory-shaped block on ORGANISATION only when nothing else committed, which never happened, because every record carries a mapped class. It had been put below class because about a third of how-blocks are inventory-shaped and the shape is a mode, not a locus: promoted alone it would make ORGANISATION the largest locus and swallow genuine SUPPLY and MANAGEMENT findings. Never firing had its own cost. A known-exploited catalogue join, reading only vuln_scan and asset_inventory and captioned 'a vulnerability management process, not a detection', sat on five loci across its 13 citing blocks by the order its records listed classes, and the copy on a web-server-first record filled the DATA slot on firewall and VPN questions. posture requires both the shape and evidence reading only posture, which is the vocabulary's ORGANISATION, 'an inventory or advice question rather than an event located on a device'. Of 267 inventory-shaped blocks, 67 read only posture: posture places 64, two sit on records listing a non-product class first and were ORGANISATION already, and one is on a supply surface that reaches it. ORGANISATION rises from 25 blocks to 89 and stays fourth of six. The two SUPPLY blocks it moves, an embedded-library inventory and a build server's patch posture, keep SUPPLY as their span from a unanimous class list, and an inventory block reading anything but posture is still placed by its class. It sits above a non-supply surface, because a posture question about the way in is still a posture question, and the surface it would have kept travels as its span. It sits below a supply surface that reaches the block, so a contract question on the supply path itself stays SUPPLY.
_why_no_evidence_tier: Until 0.43.0 an evidence tier sat between class_first and shape, placing a block by the plurality of its evidence_type. It could never fire: product_class has minItems 1 and every class is mapped, so the class tier always decided first, and the basis never printed the evidence signal either. Evidence says where a detection is READ, not where the attack sits, so it is not promoted to a tier: that would move a large share of all primaries onto the log source. It is the last span source instead, and LOCUS_BASIS always prints it. Since the 2026-10-01 third validation evidence decides inside two tiers, each narrow and each needing one deciding locus rather than a plurality: posture, an inventory-shaped block reading only posture, and admin_api_unread, a block that never reads the administrative API its first-listed class is. The fourth validation added three more, each as narrow and each placing a block only where it reads nothing on the plane it displaces: host_evidence, a block past its record's surface reading only host evidence; admin_api_listed, a record's block reading the administrative API of a class its record lists after the first; and host_listed, a record's block reading only host evidence on a record listing an endpoint class after the first. Together the five place 76 of 770 blocks: 64 by posture, 2 by admin_api_unread, 2 by admin_api_listed, 1 by host_evidence and 7 by host_listed. The tier this file rejects was measured again then, as evidence outranking any record-level plane it contradicts: it moved 129 blocks and 67 patterns and took DATA from 81 blocks to 143, 32 blocks of endpoint records onto DATA among them because they were read from proxy and flow records.
_why_host_evidence: ENDPOINT is the one locus the vocabulary defines by the evidence that reads it: execution on a host, being process, file, registry and memory, which are edr_process, edr_file, registry, memory and file_artefact. The Siemens S7 record's library-artefact block reads exactly those, on a host that is not an approved engineering workstation, cites no initial-access technique, and reads nothing on the record's management-interface surface or its PLC classes' CONTROL. surface_reaches_block kept the surface for it, because evidence on a third plane never set a surface aside, so it printed MANAGEMENT and both Siemens answers named ENDPOINT absent while their most distinctive detection is an EDR one. host_evidence sets the surface aside for such a block and places it on ENDPOINT, with the surface as its span. It places 1 block. Only host evidence decides here, measured: the same test on any single third plane also moved an SNMP-probe block read from flow and IDS records to DATA, though the vocabulary names SNMP as MANAGEMENT, and a dropped-table block read by an integrity check to SUPPLY, so the S7 record's controller sweep, read from flow and IDS records, keeps the management interface. A surface on the first-listed class's own plane always reaches, so the three host-only blocks of a VPN appliance record, whose class and portal surface are both CONTROL, stay there: an appliance has a plane decomposition. A span-only surface decides nothing and so has nothing to set aside; letting one decide a way-in block reading only its own plane was measured as a separate rule, moved 9 blocks, two AWS console-clone blocks off MANAGEMENT among them, and is the SCADA email lure's decision, not this one's. A host-only block on a record with no committing surface is host_listed's question (see _why_host_listed). A contested type is left out, so it neither decides nor stops this. validate.py counts the blocks it places.
_why_admin_api_listed: The mirror of admin_api_unread. A record listing a class in administrative_api_classes after its first names the provider whose administrative API that is, and a block reading that API, its audit trail or configuration (cloud_audit, config_diff), and nothing on its first-listed class's plane is administration of that provider, which the standing decision places on MANAGEMENT whatever the provider calls it. The AWS Kubernetes node-credentials record lists cloud.container first, and its metadata credential request paired with the node role's first cloud API call, read from flow records and the provider's audit trail, printed CONTROL: the only Amazon-named CONTROL finding, so the AWS answer claimed CONTROL coverage it does not hold. It places 2 blocks, both on that record. Restricted to administrative_api_classes, measured against two wider forms: taking the first-listed class a block reads, any class, moved 95 blocks, 38 of them from CONTROL to DATA, many on netflow alone, and an Exchange Online MailItemsAccessed block onto MANAGEMENT against _why_non_administrative_operations; taking any later-listed MANAGEMENT class moved 9, three Exchange Online forged-token blocks and two Office 365 blocks from DATA among them. A block whose cloud_operation markers are all uses of a service is never moved. Read for a record's block only: a pattern's applies_to_classes says where it applies, not which provider an incident ran through, and applied to patterns it moved 8, four of them CI/CD supply-path patterns from SUPPLY onto MANAGEMENT. Evidence on the first-listed class's plane keeps the class; a contested type neither keeps nor moves it. validate.py counts the blocks it places.
_why_host_listed: The ENDPOINT mirror of admin_api_listed. A record listing a class by_class places on ENDPOINT (endpoint.os, endpoint.browser, security.edr, security.offensive_tool, app.archiver) after its first names the host the incident ran on, and a block reading only host evidence, so nothing on its first-listed class's plane, is execution on that host: the vocabulary's ENDPOINT, whose clause that the subject is an operating system or agent the record's own class satisfies. It places 7 blocks, every one host execution: an Office document spawning a script engine after a hijacked mail thread, a credential file read at a shell on a Unix host, AI client artefacts left on disk, ransomware file activity in a model store, a directory database copy staged in a temp path, a user-scope startup property list written in an AI coding session, and a browser skimmer's in-page script read as a file artefact. They sat on CONTROL from identity.directory or app.ai_platform, or on DATA from server.mail or cloud.saas, and query-kev-growth and revoked-and-family probes named three of them. Without the listed class it was measured on 23 blocks reading only host evidence under a first-listed class on another plane. The 16 it leaves name no endpoint class (four SPIFFE workload-attestation blocks on a container and identity record, ActiveMQ, Horizon, Duo, three on a Sangoma PBX, TeamCity, Omron tooling, a Cloudflare tunnel and a Pages build, an AI-orchestrated web-server intrusion and a restricted-library container block), about half of them products with a plane decomposition, which the vocabulary's ENDPOINT excludes, so they keep their class. Read for a record's block only, as admin_api_listed is: applied to library patterns the two moved 18 patterns, 10 by this one, and lowered agreement between a pattern's locus and its citing blocks' from 481 to 478 of 755 pairs, because the SPIFFE patterns would go to ENDPOINT while their four blocks stay on CONTROL; read for blocks only they raised it from 479 to 481. An ENDPOINT-first record is class_first already. Neither a contested nor a deferred type decides or stops it. validate.py counts the blocks it places.
_tier_order: The ladder scripts/consult.py runs, in its order; the code names the same list LOCUS_TIERS. validate.py refuses the corpus when the two differ. Until 0.43.0 nothing read this list, so reversing it changed no output and failed no check.
_span_order: Where LOCUS_SPAN's second value comes from, tried in this order after the primary is decided; the first source whose locus differs from the primary wins. Every source is read from the record and its block, never from the question, so validate.py, emit_xql.py and advise.py print the second value a consultation prints for the same block. surface_span_only: a surface in surface_span_only. surface: a committing surface that did not decide, including one set aside for the block. identifier: on a generated exposure, the class plane the identifier tier displaced, or, where that tier did not decide, the plane most of its identifiers' own text reads other than the primary, ties in locus_order, a class entry reading the plane by_class gives that class (see identifier_reading). class: a unanimous class list that did not decide. nonproduct: a non-product class listed after a product class. evidence: the block's evidence_type, excluding defer_evidence, when it commits unanimously. The code names the same list LOCUS_SPAN_SOURCES and validate.py refuses the corpus when the two differ.
_class_matched: A productive class the question resolved, whose locus is neither the primary nor the record's own span, is appended to LOCUS_SPAN as a further value and the basis names it as class_matched. It is the only question-relative input. Until the 2026-09-30 validation it was the first span source and took the one span slot, so a firewall question replaced the record's own second locus with CONTROL, 238 (block, matched class) pairs dropped a second locus that way and emit_xql.py and a consultation disagreed about where the same finding sits. It now only ever adds.
_why_surface_vector_techniques: A supply surface says how the record's subject was reached, and a record carries it for every block, so it put a delivered miner's pool traffic, the IAM workload creation that followed, and SolarWinds' Golden SAML audit events on SUPPLY. Of the 73 blocks it decided, 43 had a first-listed class on another plane. It now decides only a block that detects the supply path itself: one citing the ATT&CK technique MITRE files that vector under, Supply Chain Compromise (enterprise, ICS and mobile) or Trusted Relationship, matched with its sub-techniques, or one reading integrity_check, the one evidence type that reads SUPPLY. Every other block of the record detects what the delivered code or the trusted party did afterwards, and the ladder places it as it places any block, with the supply surface carried as the span. validate.py refuses a key here that is not in surface_supply, and an id the shipped ATT&CK reference does not list, live, under initial-access.
_why_way_in_techniques: A committing surface other than a supply surface is also per record, and put every block of a record on its plane: a Siemens PLC record reached through an internet-facing management interface printed its operator-display manipulation and its S7 data-block writes, read from industrial protocol and process telemetry, on MANAGEMENT, and its AI-assisted exploit-development posture item with them, so no Siemens finding reached CONTROL. The surface now decides a block unless the block has gone past the way in: it cites none of these techniques, reads no evidence on the surface's own plane, and its evidence reads the plane of the record's first-listed class, reads only posture (asset_inventory, vuln_scan), or, since the fourth validation, reads only host evidence (edr_process, edr_file, registry, memory, file_artefact). The first two are placed by the class, the third on ENDPOINT by host_evidence (see _why_host_evidence), and each carries the surface as its span. A block citing one of these keeps the surface whatever its evidence, because it is about the way in, which is how a device-administration block read from auth_log stays on MANAGEMENT though auth_log reads CONTROL. The list is every live technique the shipped ATT&CK reference files under initial-access, parent ids, matched with their sub-techniques; validate.py refuses it when it differs from the reference, so an ATT&CK upgrade that adds or withdraws one fails until the list follows.
_why_non_administrative_operations: The operation tier places a block whose only live test is a cloud_operation on MANAGEMENT, because the vocabulary puts a cloud provider's or tenant's administrative API there whatever the provider calls it. Six blocks the tier now places sat on CONTROL or DATA because their record lists an MFA, container, AI-platform, directory or SaaS class first: an authenticator enrolled for an account, an organisation-tier policy change, SSH keys pushed into a running instance, IAM users minted for model access, an Exchange role assignment and a Microsoft 365 admin role grant. The same audit trail also records the use of a service, which is not its administration: reading mail, invoking a model, reading a stored object. A block whose every operation is listed here is not placed by the tier, which is how an Exchange Online block testing MailItemsAccessed stays on DATA. A regex, substring, prefix or suffix value is never read as listed, because it names a family of operations the list cannot enumerate. Add an operation here only when a block testing it alone would otherwise move, and say which. A library pattern placed with no block is read with its own markers the same way: until the 2026-10-01 third validation only its classes were read, so pat-mailbox-delegation-or-role-granted, whose one live test is an Exchange role or permission grant, derived DATA from server.mail while the block citing it sat on MANAGEMENT, and advise.py printed MANAGEMENT absent for a selection holding it. Reading them moved seven patterns onto MANAGEMENT. pat-mail-item-property-scan would have been an eighth, on the mailbox audit actions Update and UpdateInboxRules beside MailItemsAccessed, and declares DATA with its reason instead: its sweep reads message properties, and the actions only locate the items. Since the fourth validation a block reading only the provider's audit trail is read the same way when its operations sit beside other typed markers, which there are fields of the same audit event. The Bedrock model-access block tests model invocation beside the model-access agreement and use-case operations, with a user-name pattern and an HTTP client agent, all from CloudTrail; 0.43.0 kept it on CONTROL from app.ai_platform because those two markers are not operations, and it is now MANAGEMENT, a reversal of that recorded outcome. An S3 block testing GetCallerIdentity beside an event outcome changed tier only, MANAGEMENT either way. A process name beside host evidence is not such a field, and the listed uses still never qualify a block on their own.
_why_administrative_api_classes: vocab.json defines cloud.iaas as an infrastructure-as-a-service administrative API and console, and by_class places it on MANAGEMENT for that reason. A record about an AWS incident lists it first, and class_first then put every block of that record on MANAGEMENT, including blocks that never touch the API: a certificate issued for an owned hostname, read from DNS and TLS metadata, and a workload's sustained traffic to a mining pool, read from flow and DNS records. The AWS answer then named DATA absent while two AWS-named findings read it. admin_api_unread places such a block by its evidence when it carries no cloud_operation marker and its deciding evidence reads one locus that is neither the class's own nor posture. Reading the API in any form keeps the class: cloud_audit or config_diff, an operation marker beside other typed markers, or asset_inventory and vuln_scan, because a provider's inventory is read through its API. auth_log is not taken as the API: an IaaS provider writes a console sign-in to its audit trail, which is cloud_audit, so a block reading auth_log reads another system's sign-in. Measured, it places 2 blocks, both on DATA. cloud.identity is defined the same way and is deliberately not listed: _arguable_classes keeps it on MANAGEMENT against identity.sso on CONTROL, a tenant sign-in read from auth_log is often the administrative credential's own use, and listing it would move four blocks, an authentication-failure burst and a VPN scanning block to CONTROL and two mail-delivery blocks to DATA. That is a decision to take on its own, not a side effect of this one. validate.py refuses a listed class that by_class does not place on MANAGEMENT, and a non-product class. The list is read the other way round as well, by admin_api_listed (see _why_admin_api_listed): a record listing one of these classes after its first names the provider whose API it is. cloud.identity stays off for that direction too: added to the list it moves 9 blocks, the four above and, by admin_api_listed, two Exchange Online forged-token mailbox-access blocks and two Office 365 configuration blocks from DATA and a bulk SaaS file-access block from CONTROL, all onto MANAGEMENT.
_why_contested_evidence: process_telemetry is mapped to CONTROL on the vocabulary's reading, while the corpus also uses it for host process telemetry (_note_process_telemetry), so its locus is contested. Every test in which evidence decides anything leaves a contested type out entirely (deciding_planes in scripts/consult.py): it neither decides nor stops a decision, which keeps that note's rule that it never decides a primary. Until the fourth validation the surface reach test still read it as CONTROL, so a PLC block reading only process_telemetry under a management-interface surface was set aside onto its class's CONTROL, and an RMM block reading EDR and process_telemetry under a VPN portal kept the portal's CONTROL where its host evidence alone would have set the surface aside; the first now keeps the surface, the second sits on ENDPOINT, and no corpus block depended on either. Read either way, it held a workload's mining-pool traffic, read from flow and DNS records with the miner's process name typed process_telemetry, on MANAGEMENT from cloud.iaas, and two preparedness questions reading inventory beside process values on CONTROL. As a span source it is read as before. validate.py refuses a type here that by_evidence does not map, or that is deferred.
_why_surface_span_only: These name the way in, not the plane the detection reads. email_flow is how the lure arrived: it placed a Chrome renderer breakout, read from EDR process events, on DATA, and both Okta records on DATA while the sign-in gate they abuse is CONTROL. remote_access_service is the route an operator used: it placed a shadow-copy deletion read from EDR on MANAGEMENT. watering_hole, the web form of the same delivery vector, was already in defer_surface for this reason. Unlike a deferred surface, each still commits to a locus, and that locus is carried as a span, so the mail or remote-access relationship stays on the finding without deciding it. validate.py requires each to be mapped in by_surface and in neither defer_surface nor surface_supply.
_why_untrusted_surface_tags: An exposure carrying one of these tags was written by a generator, and its what.attack_surface was assigned, not read from any source: the KEV generator looks it up in SURFACE_BY_CLASS in _ingest/kev/generate.py, a table keyed on the first derived class, and the ZDI, PSIRT and database generators (_ingest/zdi/generate.py, _ingest/psirt/generate.py and _ingest/psirt/nvd_generate.py) import the same table. Read by the surface tier, it re-encoded the class through a remap that disagrees with by_class: network.firewall, network.router and server.hypervisor go to internet_facing_management, which this map commits to MANAGEMENT, so a firewall CVE was a management-plane finding. The surface is ignored for the ladder and the span alike, and the basis prints it as not read. A hand-written exposure carries none of these tags and its authored surface is data, read like any observation's. Each tag maps to the where.source_type its generator writes; validate.py refuses an exposure whose tag and source_type disagree, and an untagged exposure carrying one of these source types, so a generator that forgets its tag cannot have its assigned surface read as authored. Since 0.44.0 what stands in for the surface is what.identifier_signals: the generator reads each identifier's own catalogue description, advisory title or database description with identifier_reading below and records the words, so a firewall's management-interface flaw reaches MANAGEMENT by what its source says about it, never by the class table.
_why_identifier_reading: A generated exposure's class is one value for every identifier it carries, and its surface is assigned from that class, so until 0.44.0 a firewall's management-interface flaw sat on CONTROL with the rest. FortiOS's two super-admin authentication bypasses printed CONTROL beside a finding placing the same identifier on MANAGEMENT, PAN-OS's four management web interface flaws printed CONTROL alone though the record quotes the catalogue naming the interface, and 'Check Point VPN' listed none of the three identifiers the catalogue describes as VPN flaws, because no Check Point exposure carried the VPN gateway class. The generators now read each identifier's own text, in the fields named here for their tag, and write what.identifier_signals: one entry per hit, carrying the rule, the words matched and the field they came from, in what.vulnerabilities order. Within a field the earliest match in text order wins, ties in rule order, and the first field that yields one decides; the class rule is read the same way and independently, so one identifier can carry both (PAN-OS's management interface flaws affecting 'firewalls and VPN concentrators'). A locus rule names an administrative component of the product: a management or administrative interface, console, portal, panel or page, the configuration utility or backup, a super-admin account, the command-line interface, SNMP. It never reads reach, yield or mechanism: 'management network', 'administrative privileges', 'Internet Group Management Protocol' and 'observed with the CLI command:' read nothing. CLI is read in capitals only, because lower-case 'cli' hit a CGI parameter and a plugin directory. The class rule reads a remote-access VPN feature as network.vpn_gateway, and is written only on a record carrying a class beginning with class_requires_prefix and not already carrying the class it reads: unrestricted, FortiClient's VPN saved-password flaw put an endpoint agent on CONTROL and FortiPAM gained CONTROL. A rule's unless names words that put a text in another sense, and a text carrying them is not read by that rule. The vpn rule's are a provider VPN's (VRF, MPLS, L2VPN, L3VPN, EVPN, VPLS): read without them, a NetEngine router's VPN routing and forwarding (VRF) hopping flaw, CVE-2015-8087, read as a VPN gateway's, and 'Huawei VPN' listed the routers. Over the 9,915 texts in the row stores the generators read at 0.44.0, that identifier's is the only VPN text naming them. A class read this way never decides a primary, and it widens only the vendor-class exposure tier, for a vendor the question named. A class question naming no vendor is not widened: read for every question, 'VPN gateway' listed 71 class-only exposures where it lists 30. A locus every identifier reads, other than the first-listed class's, decides the primary (the identifier tier); otherwise the plane most identifiers read is the span. A record whose first product class is in undecomposed_classes is not read. The vocabulary gives ENDPOINT no plane decomposition, so the Windows Management Console and FortiClient's VPN are the endpoint itself; dev.library is listed because a library or developer tool has no administration of its own, and over the whole corpus that changes one record, 'React Native Community CLI', which read its own product name. Product names are otherwise not stripped: BIG-IP's Configuration Utility and Jenkins's Command Line Interface are named in the catalogue's product field and are the component. Measured and left out: authentication wording naming an administrator (13 more identifiers, among them Catalyst SD-WAN's peering authentication, which is control-plane session establishment, and the rule reads yield words); SSH and Telnet (4 identifiers, and the Erlang/OTP library once libraries are read); IKE as a VPN word (39 entries, 35 of them Huawei database descriptions); 'management API', 'management server' and 'management plane' (they read ISE's identity management API and product names); J-Web and an unqualified 'web UI' or 'web interface' (9 identifiers in 4 Juniper records, and 32 to 36 more, among them Pulse Connect Secure's user portal and IOS XE's Web UI); and a coordinated disclosure's specific-flaw sentence, which reads Docker Desktop's user CLI. validate.py holds every entry to this table and re-reads every catalogue description quoted by a known-exploited record the rule reads (900 across 515 records), both ways, so an entry the rule would not write, or a missing one, fails until the record is regenerated; the other 184 list an undecomposed class first and may carry no entry. A generated record carrying no key is read as carrying no entries, not skipped: until a review of 0.44.0 the re-read ran only on the 59 records carrying the field, 156 descriptions, and one whose field was dropped passed while its exposure moved plane. An advisory title or database description is quoted by no identifier anywhere in a record, so a PSIRT, coordinated-disclosure or database record's entries are held to the table only, and an entry dropped from one is not seen; nor is an identifier a catalogue record holds by identifier alone.
_why_defer_surface: These six say reachability or precondition rather than plane, and mean different things per class. A firewall's internet-facing service is forwarding; a web server's is content. A cloud API is administration; an application API is data. Committing internet_facing_service alone would put about a quarter of all blocks under one label chosen for the wrong reason.
_why_defer_evidence: Device syslog carries administrative, forwarding and payload events indifferently and commits to no locus.
_note_removable_media: Mapped but never fires: no record carries it. Kept so the vocabulary stays fully covered.
_arguable_classes: cloud.identity to MANAGEMENT splits it from identity.sso to CONTROL, and they are close to the same thing to a defender. It follows the ruling that a cloud provider's control plane is administration; tenant-admin cases reach MANAGEMENT through the surface tier anyway. ot.hmi to CONTROL reads the function rather than the host, which is a Windows box. app.version_control to SUPPLY runs against a vocabulary description that emphasises egress. security.edr to ENDPOINT places the agent, not the console -- which is exactly how two EPMM records came to derive ENDPOINT, and is why app.mdm exists as its own class. app.mdm to MANAGEMENT reads the console and the enrolment channel, never the enrolled handset: it is fleet administration holding an administrative credential for every device, which is the same reading that places app.rmm and cloud.identity. Deliberately not ENDPOINT, because the handsets are out of scope: this corpus advises on the handset OS and consumer device not at all, and on the console that enrols, configures and observes them always and aiming a management-plane finding at the endpoint plane points it at the one place this corpus declines to advise. Deliberately not CONTROL, because it makes no forwarding, session-establishment or trust-evaluation decision for traffic; where a product genuinely is a gateway, as MobileIron Sentry is, the record lists the gateway class first and app.mdm second.
_note_process_telemetry: Mapped to CONTROL on the vocabulary reading, which is process values, alarms and operator actions from the control system itself. CONNECTOR['process_telemetry'] in scripts/consult.py describes the same evidence type as host process telemetry, which is a different thing, and the blocks using it split across OT, endpoint, CI/CD and AI-platform classes, so the corpus genuinely uses it both ways. The vocabulary is the corpus contract and wins here. The contradiction is real, is not resolved by this file, and correcting the connector text either way would make it wrong for the other half of those blocks. It never decides a primary: evidence is not a tier, and every test in which evidence decides, the surface reach test included, leaves it out as contested_evidence. It can only add CONTROL as a span, and only where every other evidence type on the block agrees.
